claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
Untreated TC4 has relatively low surface hardness.
Untreated TC4 has poor friction and wear performance under high-contact-stress or extreme-service conditions.
The proposed intervention incorporates pre-placed, finely milled AlCoCrFeNi HEA particulates into the near-surface region of TC4 by friction stir processing.
The proposed FSP parameter window is 900–1100 rpm rotation speed and 80–120 mm/min traverse speed.
Inert-gas shielding will minimize oxidation during FSP.
The specified FSP parameter window will provide thorough in-situ mixing of the HEA particles into TC4.
FSP will produce a fine, dynamically recrystallized near-surface microstructure.
FSP will produce a graded near-surface region with uniformly dispersed HEA particulates embedded in the TC4 matrix.
Severe plastic deformation during FSP induces dynamic recrystallization in the near-surface region.
FSP forces intimate mechanical mixing between the TC4 matrix and pre-placed HEA particulates.
The dispersed HEA particulates act as mechanically robust reinforcement.
HEA reinforcement will increase the surface hardness of FSP-treated TC4 relative to untreated TC4.
HEA reinforcement will reduce wear and improve frictional performance relative to untreated TC4.
The proposed processing will avoid deleterious phase transformations in TC4.
Localized FSP and minimal thermal input will preserve TC4's bulk alpha-plus-beta structure and bulk properties.
The performance enhancement is expected to apply under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant hardness improvement of approximately 10–15%, together with reduced wear rate, would falsify the hypothesis.
Non-uniform HEA dispersion, excessive oxidation, or detrimental phase transformations would falsify the hypothesis.
